label: prf:binding-error-amplification
title: Proof of binding error amplification
html:
Proof. Proof of binding error amplification

Proof. By definition B^{\mathrm{pred}} - B = (M_{\mathrm{free}} - M_{\mathrm{atom}}(1+\delta)) - (M_{\mathrm{free}} - M_{\mathrm{atom}}) = -\delta\,M_{\mathrm{atom}}. Dividing by B gives -\delta\,M_{\mathrm{atom}}/B = -\delta\,(M_{\mathrm{atom}}/B). The identity is purely algebraic — it holds over any field and assumes nothing about the q-deformation, the calibration inputs, or the knot assignment. \qquad\blacksquare

The amplification factor is large precisely because binding is a small defect of two large, nearly equal masses. For the light nuclei (CODATA / AME-2020 values):

Nucleus M_{\mathrm{atom}} (MeV) B_{\mathrm{AME}} (MeV) \mathcal{A} = M_{\mathrm{atom}}/B
{}^2\mathrm{H} \approx 1875.6 \approx 2.225 \approx 843
{}^3\mathrm{H} \approx 2808.9 \approx 8.482 \approx 331
{}^3\mathrm{He} \approx 2808.4 \approx 7.718 \approx 364
{}^4\mathrm{He} \approx 3727.4 \approx 28.296 \approx 132

A bound-state mass predicted to 0.1\% — already a demanding target for the per-knot mass formula \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathfrak{m}_e\,\mathrm{Vol}(K)\,\varrho(K)/\hbar_q^2 — therefore yields a binding energy wrong by tens of percent (0.1\% \times 843 \approx 84\% for the deuteron). The amplification is worst for the lightest, most weakly bound nuclei.

Corollary. The per-knot mass-prediction accuracy and the binding-energy accuracy are not independent problems. Binding is the amplified shadow of the bound-state mass error: any residual in the predicted nuclear mass is magnified by \mathcal{A} in the binding. A categorical derivation of binding to experimental precision therefore requires the bound-state mass to be derived to a precision finer than B/M_{\mathrm{atom}} \approx 0.1\%–0.8\% of the experimental binding target.

This also explains why computing binding as a difference of two large Markov traces \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\mathrm{free}}) - \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\mathrm{atom}}) is canonical hostile: it subjects the small binding signal to the same catastrophic cancellation, so any systematic in the trace is magnified by \mathcal{A}. Forming the difference object before evaluating — so that binding is computed as a single quantity rather than a cancellation of two large ones — is the structural way to avoid the amplification.
